sub_answers.sub_question: List and quantify the distinct revenue streams for Belgian first-division clubs and UEFA participants (e.g., Royal Antwerp): UEFA competition prize money breakdown, domestic league prize pools, TV/broadcast distribution formulas (domestic and Champions/Europa Conference League), UEFA coefficient-related payouts, solidarity payments, and typical commercial matchday and academy-related income — include typical ranges or examples from similar clubs.
sub_answers.text: UEFA club competition payments are allocated through match/round points and bonus points, with clubs receiving two points for a win and one point for a draw in the main stages and additional bonus points for entering/advancing in Champions League group and knockout phases [d1800094s9p0]. UEFA club coefficient is calculated as the sum of points earned by the club in UEFA competitions over the previous five seasons or 20% of the association coefficient over the same period, whichever is higher, which affects seeding and therefore potential draw difficulty and match-related revenues [d1800094s9p0]. The association coefficient, driven by clubs’ UEFA results over five seasons and averaged per participating team, determines how many clubs from an association enter UEFA competitions and thus affects aggregate UEFA revenue flow to clubs in that association [d1800094s1p0]. UEFA competition structure and automatic qualification slots (e.g., Champions League league-phase access for top-ranked associations) shape which clubs gain direct league-phase revenues versus those needing qualifying rounds, affecting revenue certainty [d1800094s1p0]. Participation in the UEFA Conference League carries an access/reward pathway including an automatic Europa League place for the winners, which alters medium-term revenue prospects for participating clubs [d76204273s0p0].
